summary: Raleigh County lookout near Kingston: station 1916-21, tower chopped down before 1926, steel replacement 1961 per register; listed gone, no site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the association; no source found that describes the site now

events.note: Luther Proffit placed on duty as temporary watchman; station completed that summer (1916 state report)
Register gives 1921 for the original tower; a 1921 notice gives May 10, 1921 for the station's completion. The sources do not agree on the first opening (see 1916)
Tower found chopped down; $500 reward offered (item dated April 9, 1926)
Observer Ira Sowder at the tower; observer and son built a windmill for power
Register: a steel tower replaced the original

notes_for_editor: Height not used in facts. The record's height_m 18.3 (60 ft) is not in the text read: the 1926 item proposes a 60-foot steel tower and the 1985 item says 50 feet. Opening date conflict: 1916 state report (completed that summer) vs 1921 (register and notice); the event is recorded as built 1921 with the conflict in the note. The 1985 item (3,250-ft ridge, 50-ft tower) does not match the 3,150-ft site and may describe another structure; the story says the link is unclear. County: the record and FFLA say Raleigh; some map sites say Fayette; sources describe the Raleigh/Fayette line. A firelookout.org PDF by Pop Wriston (pop-wriston-built-the-big-ones.pdf) turned up in search and may cover this tower; it is a scan with no text layer and was not read, so nothing from it is used. The FFLOS photo (credit Ronnie Scarbro, all rights reserved in record) is not added. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story's 'join the station to the private line' wording went beyond the source (the source says the line connects with the Solvay private line) and was rewritten. The April 1926 item and the June 1921 American Forestry notice are now cited by their dates and attributions. Note: the April 9, 1926 item and the October 10, 1926 Charleston Gazette item both place the Kingston tower in Fayette County, while the 1916 report places it in Raleigh County; the story attributes Raleigh only to the 1916 report.
